title: The deep learning and transformer era

sources.claim: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton (NeurIPS 2012): a deep convolutional network trained on GPUs won the ILSVRC-2012 image-recognition competition with a top-5 error of 15.3 percent versus 26.2 percent for the next entry, a result widely seen as a turning point for deep learning.

Vaswani et al. (2017), "Attention Is All You Need", introduced the Transformer, a network built on attention without recurrence, first posted in June 2017; transformers became the basis of most later large language models.
OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview on November 30, 2022, which brought chat-style access to a large language model to a very wide public.

questions.intro: Three milestones show the deep learning era. In 2012, a deep neural network trained on graphics processors (GPUs), often called AlexNet, won a major image-recognition competition with a top-5 error of 15.3 percent versus 26.2 percent for the next entry. In 2017, the paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduced the TRANSFORMER, a design that became the basis of most later large language models. On November 30, 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview, bringing chat-style access to a large language model to a very wide public.

sections.skill: Compare the milestones with the history of cars

questions.domain: Society: history and claims about the future
questions.prompt: The 2012 result is most like which car stage?

choices.text: Affordable cars for ordinary families, since 2012 was when everyone started using AI

questions.intro: Cars changed in stages. A better ENGINE made cars powerful. A better DESIGN, such as the assembly line, made them practical to build at scale. Then affordable models put cars in ORDINARY FAMILIES' hands. AI's recent history has similar stages: 2012 showed deep networks were powerful, 2017 gave a design that scaled, and 2022 put chat-style AI in ordinary people's hands.

sections.skill: See what each milestone changed and what it raised

questions.domain: Society: history and claims about the future
questions.prompt: What did 2012 show?

choices.text: Deep networks plus data and computing could beat older methods
That deep networks would never be useful for any task

questions.correct_answer: Deep networks plus data and computing could beat older methods
questions.intro: Each milestone changed something different. 2012 showed that deep networks plus lots of data and computing power could beat older methods on a hard task. 2017 gave a design that scaled well to huge amounts of text. 2022 changed who used the technology, putting it in everyday hands. None of these happened alone: they built on decades of earlier research, and each brought new questions about accuracy, cost and fairness.
